standard_prerequisites: the naively trivialized cotangent complex NL of a presentation and its behaviour under base change
the two categories of the chapter and the rings B_n = B/I^nB, A_n
homotopy limits Rlim of inverse systems of complexes and pro-isomorphic systems
core_obligations: Prove that the pro-objects formed by the reductions NL^wedge_{B/A} tensor B/I^nB and by NL_{B_n/A_n} are strictly isomorphic, and that NL^wedge_{B/A} equals Rlim NL_{B_n/A_n} in D(B)
proof_roadmap: Fix a presentation B = A[x_1,...,x_r]^wedge/J; it induces presentations B_n = A_n[x_1,...,x_r]/J_n with J_n the extension of J
The two-term complex J_n/J_n^2 to the free module on dx_i represents NL_{B_n/A_n}

Artin-Rees in the Noetherian completion ring gives c and canonical surjections J/I^nJ to J_n to J/I^{n-c}J to J_{n-c}; these are compatible with the differentials and yield maps of complexes NL^wedge tensor B/I^nB to NL_{B_n/A_n} to NL^wedge tensor B/I^{n-c}B to NL_{B_{n-c}/A_{n-c}} compatible with the transition maps, which proves strict pro-isomorphism

Since pro-isomorphic systems have the same Rlim, it remains to show NL^wedge_{B/A} is the Rlim of its own reductions; it is a two-term complex of finite I-adically complete B-modules, for which the module Rlim computation gives M = lim M/I^nM = Rlim M/I^nM
difficulty_reason: H2: the Artin-Rees truncation comparison is the technical heart and is written out with the explicit four-term chain of surjections; the derived-limit half is a standard completeness argument for finite modules.
